original_question: Is it consistent that for some weakly compact cardinal κ that is not measurable, every 2-coloring of κ^+ × κ has a monochromatic rectangle of sizes κ^+ and κ, i.e. \( inom{\kappa^+}{\kappa} 	o  inom{\kappa^+}{\kappa}^{1,1}_2\)?
target_in_paper: Section 3, Problem 3.4: the consistency of the strong polarized relation \binom{\kappa^+}{\kappa} \to \binom{\kappa^+}{\kappa}^{1,1}_2 for a weakly compact cardinal \kappa that is not measurable.
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper’s intended target almost exactly: it has the right cardinal pair (\kappa^+,\kappa), the right positive polarized partition relation, the right number of colors (2), and the right large-cardinal profile (weakly compact but not measurable). It is clearly aiming at the paper’s specific open problem rather than a neighboring result.
missing_details: State explicitly that this is a consistency question, i.e. whether there is a model of ZFC (typically a forcing extension) with such a cardinal \kappa and such a partition relation.
Name the relation as the strong polarized relation, which is the paper’s official terminology.

Unpack the partition notation using Definition 0.1: for every coloring c: \kappa^+ \times \kappa \to 2, there must exist A \subseteq \kappa^+ and B \subseteq \kappa with |A| = \kappa^+ and |B| = \kappa such that c is constant on A \times B.
Make explicit that weak compactness and nonmeasurability are properties of the same witnessing cardinal \kappa in the model under discussion.
refined_question: Is it consistent that there exists a cardinal \kappa such that \kappa is weakly compact but not measurable and the strong polarized relation \binom{\kappa^+}{\kappa} \to \binom{\kappa^+}{\kappa}^{1,1}_2 holds; that is, for every coloring c: \kappa^+ \times \kappa \to 2 there are sets A \subseteq \kappa^+ and B \subseteq \kappa with |A| = \kappa^+ and |B| = \kappa such that c is constant on A \times B?
justification: The draft is targeting Section 3, Problem 3.4 essentially verbatim, not the neighboring questions about the pair (2^\kappa,\kappa) in Problems 3.1-3.3 and not the negative ZFC question in Problem 3.5. Definition 0.1 supplies the exact meaning of the arrow notation as a monochromatic rectangle for every 2-coloring. The immediate context before Problem 3.4 explains why this question is natural: Theorem 1.6 gives a route to the positive relation from \kappa^+ < \mathfrak{s}_\kappa, and the paper then notes that the consistency of \mathfrak{s}_\kappa > \kappa^+ already requires \kappa to be weakly compact, motivating the sharper question of whether weak compactness without measurability is enough.
